newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin expresses confidence in new government.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin expresses confidence in new government.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin expressed confidence in the pro-reform Russian government formed in March during a meeting on Monday with First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais, Russian media reported.

"I am happy with your many draft decrees and resolutions. They are fresh and not at all like earlier ones," Interfax news agency quoted Yeltsin as telling Chubais, who oversees Russian economic policymaking.

Saying the previous cabinet was stagnating, Yeltsin said the new team -- in which young reformer Boris Nemtsov is the other First Deputy Prime Minister -- "had positively affected the style, methods and results" of the government's work.
But Yeltsin stressed the need for results in a country still suffering from an economic depression with many workers receiving salaries months behind schedule.
"Now already we need to think about results, how to fulfill everything that's been planned," Yeltsin said.
He said the most pressing short-term goal is paying off back wages and pensions by July 1, Itar-Tass news agency reported.

Yeltsin, 66, who returned to active work in January after eight months of illness, formed an effectively new government under veteran Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and entrusted it with reviving market reforms.
Chubais and Nemtsov are the driving force in the new government and, with full presidential support, appear to have a free hand -- at least for now.
The president made the remarks as the government faces another possible confrontation with a parliament dominated by communists and nationalists.
On Wednesday, the State Duma lower house of parliament is due to review the government's request to cut spending on the current budget since tax revenues have fallen far short of expectations.
The topic was among issues discussed by Yeltsin and Chubais, the Kremlin in a statement.
Also on Monday, Yeltsin met Defence Minister Igor Sergeyev. The president appointed Sergeyev last month after sacking his predecessor for failing to proceed fast enough with military reforms.
In a day packed with meetings, Yeltsin also met the head of the border guard service Andrei Nikolayev, as well as the speaker of the regional parliament in Dagestan, Russian media reported.
